subject: Term sheet: Dedicated capacity increase & autoscale commitments
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecloud.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-25T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning: capacity + autoscale commitments

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the renewal reminder last week. We reviewed our usage and expect a 2.4x increase in peak inference traffic over the next 12 months as we ramp a new feature. We want to lock additional dedicated capacity as part of the renewal and also align on autoscale guardrails so our SLAs hold during promo spikes.

High-level asks from Eng/Procurement:
- Reserve +12 A100 equivalent GPUs on Dedicated for year+term (prefer reserved pool with warm standby).
- Min/max replica bounds we can rely on for capacity planning (we'd like a firm min for baseline throughput).
- A short scale-up lag commitment (we're trying to avoid 60s cold-start windows).
- A throughput / latency commitment for the pinned capacity (p95 inference latency <= 350ms at 60 concurrent requests).

Procurement will want the amendment for review (attached: acme_capacity_request.xlsx). Can your team propose concrete min/max/warm-pool numbers and a pricing uplift for the additional reserved GPUs? Also please include an operational playbook for how Redwood performs ramp/fallback during regional capacity shortfalls.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Product
Acme Cloud

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-29T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: capacity + autoscale commitments

Samantha / Olga / Marissa — technical note from infra side. Below are three options we recommend with tradeoffs called out. These are tuned for typical seq-length=512 request profiles; we'll re-bench if Acme's runtime differs substantially.

Option A — Conservative (lower cost, slower scale):
- Reserved GPUs: +12 A100-eq
- Min replicas: 4
- Max replicas: 24
- Warm pool size: 4 (keeps 4 machines KV-warmed)
- Scale-up target (cold->ready): 45s median (due to container spin + model load)
- SLA note: p95 latency <= 400ms at 50 concurrent

Option B — Balanced (recommended for fast ramp + cost predictability):
- Reserved GPUs: +12 A100-eq (in reserved pool), plus elastic burst for 8 more if needed
- Min replicas: 6
- Max replicas: 30
- Warm pool size: 6
- Scale-up target: 25–30s median with continuous background prefetching of the most common model variants
- SLA note: p95 latency <= 350ms at 60 concurrent

Option C — Aggressive (higher cost, tight latency):
- Reserved GPUs: +12 A100-eq pinned (no burst), plus +6 hot standby on warm-standby machines
- Min replicas: 8
- Max replicas: 36
- Warm pool size: 8
- Scale-up target: ~15–20s with pre-warmed partial KV cache; suitable for launch windows
- SLA note: p95 latency <= 300ms at 80 concurrent

Operational considerations:
- Warm pool is implemented as pre-warmed containers with KV cache primed for the top 10 prompts; fully loading a new model instance still adds ~1–2s for kv population depending on context window.
- We can provide an autoscale playbook covering: throttling thresholds, graceful fallback (route to hosted API variant), and priority routing for high-tier customers.

I'll attach a sample YAML that maps these parameters into a Dedicated autoscale policy for your SRE/Procurement to review.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood

Date: 2027-04-01T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Acme redlines: Amendment review

Olga / Redwood team — attached is the procurement redline of the amendment (Acme_AMENDMENT_redline.docx). A few points to call out:
- We appreciate the warm pool language. Procurement is pushing for a maximum scale-up lag clause of 20s for incidents that qualify as "business-critical" (we can define triggering thresholds).
- We want the throughput commitment expressed as "sustained concurrent request handling at p95" with a measurement window of 5m.
- On reserved hardware: procurement prefers pricing with a step-down credit if sustained usage does not hit 70% of committed capacity for a 60-day window.

Samantha and I will be the primary touchpoints for redline questions. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the 20s cap for business-critical windows or provide an alternative mitigation (e.g., pre-warm callback or prioritized warm pool).

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Procurement Manager
Acme Cloud

[attachment: Acme_AMENDMENT_redline.docx (docx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <procurement@acmecloud.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme redlines: Amendment review

Evan / Samantha — quick internal check-in before we send a formal counter:
- Pricing: we can support the reserved +12 GPUs at a +37% uplift to current committed rates (volume discount included). We'll model a step-down credit for long-term underutilization; legal needs a concrete threshold table but commercial is OK to include a 60-day lookback at 70% utilization to trigger partial credit.
- 20s scale-up for "business-critical" windows: Karthik's engineering note — guaranteed 20s is tough at large cold-model loads unless we accept higher warm-pool reservation. Proposed contract approach:
  * Baseline guarantee: 30s median scale-up for regular windows (Option B numbers).
  * Business-critical guarantee: 20s max if Acme purchases the +2 hot standby machines (adds ~6% to reserved cost) and agrees to run a short daily simulated warm call to keep KV primed for FR1 prompts.
- We'll include an operational runbook and a monitoring hook that surfaces warm-pool utilization and scale-up latency to Acme's console.

Marissa (CS) will produce a term-sheet PDF with the two tracks (standard vs business-critical). Olga will send the DocuSign once we have your confirmation on the hot-standby add-on.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood

Subject: Final term sheet & next steps (DocuSign link)

Samantha / Evan — attaching the term sheet and operational appendix for signature. Summary of agreed options:

Agreed commercial summary:
- Reserved capacity: +12 A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool) for 12 months, + option to convert 2 of those to hot-standby for business-critical windows.
- Price uplift: +37% over current committed rates for reserved +12; hot-standby option adds +6% to uplift.
- Utilization protection: 60-day lookback at 70% usage threshold to trigger step-down credit (detailed in the amendment).

Autoscale & SLOs:
- Baseline policy (Option B): min_replicas=6, max_replicas=30, warm_pool_size=6, scale_up_median=25–30s, SLA: p95 latency <= 350ms at 60 concurrent requests.
- Business-critical option: with +2 hot-standby machines and a brief daily warm callback, Redwood will commit to max scale-up 20s for qualifying windows. Triggering criteria and simulation cadence are in the appendix.

Operational items included:
- acme_autoscale_config.yaml (maps options A/B/C to actual Dedicated config).
- Monitoring links and playbook: warm-pool utilization dashboard, token-level cost traces, and fallback routing to hosted API variant in the rare event of regional capacity shortages.

Please review and sign via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/ACME-Doc-Invite-789. If you want a 30-minute call to walk the appendix prior to signing, I'm available tomorrow at 09:00 or 13:00 PT.

Thanks for the partnership — excited to support your launch.

Olga Petrov
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
